VON SOLLE

ELSEVIER
The logo for Elsevier, which consists of an illustration of a man standing under a tree with a banner containing the text 'NON SOLUS', with the word 'ELSEVIER' written in a serif font below the illustration.


Contents lists available at ScienceDirect

Midwifery


Midwifery AN INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL
This is the cover page for the journal *Midwifery*, Volume 24, Issue 3, September 2008. It lists the following article titles: 1. *The challenge of evidence-based midwifery: a review of the literature*; 2. *Midwifery in India: a study of status and challenges in rural Rajasthan, India*; 3. *Predictors of postnatal depression in mothers of infants in the neonatal unit*; 4. *A survey of the clinical practice of midwifery in the United Kingdom and Ireland: a study of the role of the midwife*; 5. *The importance of 'Midwifery' today: the changing landscape of maternity care and what this means for midwives*; 6. *A comparison of traditional prenatal care in pregnancy clinics and the experiences of women during labour*; 7. *The efficacy of midwifery care models: a review of the evidence*; 8. *The personal and professional development of midwives*; 9. *The role of the midwife in the 21st century*; 10. *Trends in midwifery in the United Kingdom: a review of the literature*; 11. *Reflections on the role of the midwife in the 21st century*; 12. *Using evidence-based practice in daily midwifery*; 13. *The role of the midwife in the modern health care system: a review of the literature*; 14. *A study of the experiences of English midwives who work as private practitioners*.


journal homepage: www.elsevier.com/locate/midw

Corrigendum

Corrigendum to "Midwifery continuity of carer in an area of high socio- economic disadvantage in London: A retrospective analysis of Albany Midwifery Practice outcomes using routine data (1997-2009)" [Midwifery 48 (2017) 1-10]

Caroline S.E. Homer, RM, MMed(ClinEpi), PhD Professorª,*, Nicky Leap, DMid Adjunct Professor of Midwiferyª, Nadine Edwards, PhD Independent Researchera,b,c, Jane Sandall, PhD, CBE Professor, NIHR Senior Investigatorb,c

a Centre for Midwifery, Child and Family Health, Faculty of Health, University of Technology Sydney, PO Box 123, Broadway, Sydney, New South Wales 2007, Australia

b Division of Women's Health, Faculty of Life Sciences & Medicine, King's College London, United Kingdom

" Women's Health Academic Centre, St. Thomas' Hospital, London SE1 7EH, United Kingdom

The authors regret that on page 8 we inadvertently referred to NICE as providing policy and policy direction. This was incorrect. NICE provides national clinical guidance based on systematic reviews. The sentence should read: A large study comparing perinatal outcomes by planned place of birth (Birthplace in England Collaborative Group, 2011) supported the clinical guidance to offer women with low risk pregnancies a choice of birth settings, including birth at home (NICE, 2014).

The authors would like to apologise for any inconvenience caused.

DOI of original article: http://dx.doi.org/10.1016/j.midw.2017.02.009

Corresponding author.

E-mail address: caroline.homer@uts.edu.au (C.S.E. Homer).

http://dx.doi.org/10.1016/j.midw.2017.05.013

Please cite this article as: Homer, C., Midwifery (2017), http://dx.doi.org/10.1016/j.midw.2017.05.013
